snippet.title: A palette of colors is better than just one | Sepanta Molaei | TEDxDAA Youth
snippet.description:
Can you think about the last time you really acknowledged the colour of your skin? I mean, really acknowledged; what difference would it make if I were a different color? Would everyone treat me differently?
Is our world truly equal? Or are we ignoring the hidden but visible problem? In this talk, Sepanta digs deep into mind-altering impacts of prejudice and racism, arising from his experience of identity crisis. Sepanta explores the mindset that combats prejudice.  Sepanta is a Grade 11 student from Canada who is interested in social sciences and humanities. He has always had an interest in how societies operate and interact with each other. Alongside his interest in history, Sepanta developed a passion for real world issues such as racism and prejudice, where he utilizes his knowledge of societies and history as well as personal experiences to dig deeper into prejudice and how it can be dealt with. snippet.description:

Does your dog follow you to the bathroom, wait outside the door, or trail behind you from room to room? It may look sweet, but it does not always mean the same thing.

Your dog may see you as their safe base, expect attention, follow your routine, feel bored, or look for comfort when they are scared. Sometimes, constant following can also be one sign of separation anxiety.

snippet.title: Most Dog Bites Start With These 16 Overlooked Warning Signs
snippet.description:
🎁🎁 Your gift is here ➡️ https://happydogsplace.com/gift/



Many dog bites don’t happen out of the blue. In most cases, the dog has been showing warning signs for a while, signs we often miss or don’t fully understand.

That’s why in this video I explain 16 canine body language signals that commonly appear before a conflict, from very subtle gestures to clear warnings.

This isn’t about being afraid of dogs or distrusting them. It’s about learning how to read them better, respect their boundaries, and respond in time.

If you live with dogs, have kids around, or interact with dogs regularly, this video can help you avoid scary situations and improve everyday life with dogs.


____________________
⚠️ All of these signals are your dog’s way of communicating, not misbehaving. They’re not being stubborn, dramatic, or “bad.” They’re trying to tell you that something doesn’t feel right, that they’re uncomfortable, overwhelmed, or unsure about what’s happening.

For dogs, body language is the warning system. It’s how they ask for space, time, or a different approach. When we get frustrated or punish these signals, we don’t fix the problem, we just silence the warning.

What actually helps is slowing things down, lowering the pressure, and listening to what the dog is telling us in that moment.

The goal isn’t to control the dog, it’s to understand them. And when we do, we don’t just prevent scary situations, we build trust and make everyday life safer and calmer for everyone involved.
____________________

snippet.title: Why Your Prong Collar Stops Working
snippet.description:
The prong collar is a communication tool—not something that should be constantly active.

If your dog is feeling pressure every second of every walk, they begin to tune it out. The more they become desensitized to the sensation, the less effective it becomes when you actually need to communicate something important.

Use the prong collar with intention, not as background noise. Clear communication always beats constant pressure.

snippet.title: NEXUS ERGO SUM : Réapprendre à se connecter à la terre et aux vivants | Frédéric REVOL | TEDxSaclay
snippet.description: Paysan, agriculteur biologique et distillateur, Frédéric questionne l'un des grands récits qui guide nos sociétés depuis des millénaires : celui d'une humanité engagée sur une trajectoire de progrès, de performance et de croissance, persuadée d'être séparée du reste du vivant et de pouvoir façonner le monde pour elle-même, jusqu'à en dépasser les limites. Son installation en agriculture biologique pour produire ses whiskys marque une véritable crise existentielle qui l'amène à réinterroger cette posture prométhéenne. En prenant ses distances avec l'agro-industrie, il découvre que la fertilité de sa ferme comme la qualité de ses whiskys sont le fruit de l'alliance d'un vaste écosystème – sols, micro-organismes, champignons, faune et flore – dont il est lui-même l'un des protagonistes. Son expérience lui révèle que la réussite ne naît ni de la seule volonté humaine ni de la maîtrise de la nature, mais des relations écologiques et des conversations sensibles que nous entretenons avec le vivant, y compris avec des êtres dont nous ignorons souvent jusqu'à l'existence. Ingénieur agronome et économiste de formation, Frédéric a d’abord consacré sa carrière à l’étude des enjeux d’écologie et des territoires. Convaincu que les modèles ne suffisent pas à comprendre le vivant, il choisit de devenir paysan et reprend une ferme de montagne dans les Alpes. Il la convertit à l’agriculture biologique et développe une approche agronomique frugale, fondée sur les équilibres écologiques. Fondateur du Domaine des Hautes Glaces, il crée des whiskies d’exception conçus comme des grands crus, révélant l’expression d’un territoire vivant. Son parcours l’a conduit à une conviction : la transition écologique se joue autant dans nos choix intimes que dans nos innovations, en réconciliant savoir, sensibilité et vivant. Can we really create a world where we can peacefully coexist with them using the same tool that caused the very cruelty that we don’t want?
